text:
Brief for Team TS3012 before meeting TS3012d (based on TS3012a, TS3012b, TS3012c).

WHAT HAS BEEN DECIDED (CURRENT)
- The product is aimed at younger people, which remains the main goal. The deluxe edition includes an LCD screen and speech recognition, and the case is rubber. [TS3012c: "We're definitely focussing on the younger people, 'cause that was our main goal."] [TS3012c: "I think we'll I think we're going towards the deluxe edition anyway, because that seems to be what the people want."] [TS3012c: "That's small. So we can implement it. So why why if it's small and we can imp why shouldn't we?"]
- Energy comes from regular batteries; kinetic and solar options were dropped and no rechargeable module is offered. The chip must be advanced to support the LCD and advanced features. [TS3012c: "Uh energy, we choose regular regular batteries. The chip is advanced because we have the advanced features."] [TS3012c: "Well, mm it's not in the list. So we cannot choose from it. So"] [TS3012c: "The chip is advanced because we have the advanced features."]
- The beep and a flashing light help recover a lost remote, and the channel selection uses push-buttons instead of a scroll-wheel, which was cancelled. [TS3012c: "we are going to implement the beep and the flash thing to recover your remote."] [TS3012c: "I think a push-button for channel would be better."] [TS3012c: "No r no scroll-wheel. Okay. Um I don't see anything missing really."]
- The remote is universal, not only a TV remote, and has few buttons with the most used functions placed for the thumb. The shape is leaner with softened corners. [TS3012b: "I think we should go for universal, because apparently we're a separate company making separate c remote controls to sell to a lot of diverse people."] [TS3012c: "For zapping, cau because people are zapping most of the time."] [TS3012c: "I think so because it looks leaner and we should just go with that."]
- The teletext button stays as a less prominent extra key next to mute, and changeable covers are not part of the basic design. [TS3012c: "The left one is teletext and the right one is mute."] [TS3012c: "If we wanna expand our options, f be fashionable, then we can get changeable covers."]

WHAT CHANGED ALONG THE WAY
- Speech recognition was first excluded for maturity, memory and multi-language reasons, but is now included in the deluxe design because the component is small and people want it. [TS3012b: "I don't think it should be implemented in a remote control yet uh."] [TS3012c: "That's small. So we can implement it. So why why if it's small and we can imp why shouldn't we?"]
- The LCD screen moved from a conditional proposal to inclusion in the deluxe edition, as the team moves towards deluxe. [TS3012b: "if it's not too expensive, we should include it"] [TS3012c: "I think we'll I think we're going towards the deluxe edition anyway, because that seems to be what the people want."]
- Changeable covers moved from a proposal to sell a basic remote with separate covers to a decision to leave them out of the basic design for now. [TS3012b: "So you don't have to I think you don't have to make entire remote controls."] [TS3012c: "If we wanna expand our options, f be fashionable, then we can get changeable covers."]
- The lost-remote light moved from a proposal for deaf users to a beep plus flashing light that is implemented. [TS3012b: "Perhaps we should also make uh something like a flash on it, if you if it's lost, for people that are deaf."] [TS3012c: "we are going to implement the beep and the flash thing to recover your remote."]
- Advanced functions moved from a second-level menu to navigation through the LCD screen menu, which is still open. [TS3012b: "maybe a second second level menu for the advanced things."] [TS3012c: "the advanced option could also be integrated in the L_C_D_ screen, of course, because you don't have to have a button for everything."]
- The remote shape changed from a distinct curved shape to a leaner shape with softened corners and a rounded top. [TS3012b: "I think it should be a little distinct from everything else"] [TS3012c: "I think so because it looks leaner and we should just go with that."]

OPEN ACTIONS AND OWNERS
- Speaker D (Marketing Expert) will look up the exact percentage of people who want voice recognition before the next meeting. [TS3012c: "Yeah. Mean of uh seventy percent I think. Uh I'm I have to look it up."]
- Speaker B and Speaker C work on the final internal and external design, while Speaker D finds out how the product will fall into the market. [TS3012c: "apparently you guys, you should work together on the final design, both on internal and external design."]
- Speaker D (Marketing Expert) has marketing ideas to develop individually before the next meeting. [TS3012a: "Um no, not really yet, but I've some ideas and I will uh"]
- Speaker C (Industrial Designer) is studying materials for cost and will find out whether a docking or recharging solution is possible and what it costs. [TS3012b: "Uh material study, I'm working on that um for the the costs."] [TS3012b: "Yes. I'm going to try to find that out."]
- Speaker A (Project Manager) will research whether the remote can open the TV's advanced menu. [TS3012b: "we need to put some research into that if if we can open the menu"]
- Everyone should propose a product name rather than a serial number. [TS3012b: "let's give this uh a name, and not like some vague serial number that no one understands"]

DISAGREEMENTS AND QUESTIONS STILL OPEN
- The corporate colour and slogan are unsettled: Speaker C (Industrial Designer) wants a yellow remote with black buttons, Speaker B (User Interface Designer) prefers a neutral base colour because of covers, and Speaker A (Project Manager) leans to black and yellow. [TS3012c: "It's either black cover with yellow buttons or vice versa."]
- The speech recognition microphone placement (top, side, or double) is still open, and the transmitter location may cause interference. [TS3012c: "Um yeah, it could be either be here or make a double microphone."]
- Speaker A (Project Manager) questions whether the product should be usable by disabled users, and whether truly disabled users would be a problem. [TS3012a: "Do we want people who are disabled in any way to uh, yeah, to be able to use it as well?"]
- Speaker B (User Interface Designer) notes that the budget is limited relative to the selling price target. [TS3012a: "Okay, well that's not that much to work with."]
- Whether customers value a rechargeable battery and would pay extra for it still needs to be found out. [TS3012b: "I'm not sure, you should find out if it's if rechargeable is important."]
- Speaker A objects to the kinetic energy option because remotes lie still most of the time and generate too little power. [TS3012c: "I'm sure t I mean remotes lie still I think like ninety nine percent of the time."]
